text.p: Nigerian equities closed higher on Thursday, buoyed by growing buying interest in stocks, dealers said.
The all-share index rose to 7364.25 from 7334.11 on Wednesday, helped by big gains in several sectors.
"Improved trading results have helped to brighten investors perception of the market," one trader said.
Stocks seen benefitting most included leading banks that have announced better results and those expected to follow suit in the next few weeks.
"A recent government order on banks to increase their capital base nine-fold has also boosted trading in the sector as investors are buying in anticipation of scrip issues," said one trader.
Afribank, the fourth largest bank, soared 23 kobo, the maximum five percent movement allowed daily, to 4.83 naira. The nations big three ahead of it also closed higher.
Traders said conglomerates witnessed increased activity on Thursday despite continued offloading of PZ Industries which slid 10 kobo to 27.40 naira.
Shares of Lever Brothers and UAC were 10 kobo higher, respectively, at 17.40 naira and 9.60 naira.
A.G. Leventis went nine kobo up to 1.99 naira and resurgent Franco-Nigerian concern CFAO added two kobo to 2.52 naira.

Food companies Nestle advanced 20 kobo to 58,00 naira and Nigerian Bottling Company notched 30 kobo to 38.30 naira while construction firms Cappa & DAlberto and Impresit Bakolori went five kobo up at 8.47 naira and 3.50 naira, respectively.
Oil shares remained strong. Total, at 65.80 naira, and Unipetrol, at 68.90 naira, added 25 kobo each.
But brewers closed weaker as sellers continued to dump their shares. Guinness slid 10 kobo to 7.60 naira and Nigerian Breweries dropped two kobo to end at 15.80 naira.
Benue Cement, at 6.35 naira, shed 15 kobo, and African Paints went one kobo lower at 1.52 naira.
